title: Soft Rollout Susceptibility Matrix + Hourglass Timetable (Nov 2026)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft for running constrained, soft rollouts of user-facing inference changes (model variant swaps, KV cache behavior changes, batching policy tweaks). The goal is to provide an operational susceptibility matrix (what fails first and why), an hourglass-style timetable for phased traffic ramp and unwind, and a concise release notes draft and fallout response checklist.

Audience:
Release engineers, SREs, serving runtime owners, product QA, solutions eng on-call.

Background/context:
- Target change: introduce new quantization profile (q8-dyn) for open-model-xyz and enable adaptive batching window extension for low-latency customers.
- Why soft rollout: expected single-digit percent P50 latency improvements but unknown tail behavior for some customer workloads (long prompts + function calls). We must minimize user-visible errors and preserve SLOs for Dedicated customers.

Susceptibility matrix (high level) — what can go wrong and early signals:
- KV cache regressions
  - Cause: new kernel selection path mishandles larger KV sizes for certain model layers.
  - Early signals: per-request tokenization-size > historical 99th percentile; sudden increase in latency (>30% over baseline) on prefix-heavy requests.
  - Metric to watch: percent of requests with KV cache eviction > baseline by +10bps.
  - Mitigation: automatic fallback to previous kernel within 90s; route traffic to compatibility model variant.

- Quantization numeric drift (quality)
  - Cause: q8-dyn rounding causing hallucination changes for constrained contexts.
  - Early signals: automated eval set (10 carefully curated prompts) shows BLEU/ROUGE-like drop or prompt-specific score delta > threshold.
  - Metric: model-eval-quality-regression (run per build) and customer-reported semantic-diff score > 0.12.
  - Mitigation: immediate pin to earlier quant profile; flag customers for manual rollback.

- Adaptive batching latency outliers
  - Cause: extension of batching window increases tail latency for low-concurrency, high-priority routes.
  - Early signals: P95 spike for routes with tps < 2.0; increase in 5xx transient errors from runtime queue overload.
  - Metric: route.P95_latency_ms and runtime.queue_length_percentile_99.
  - Mitigation: revert adaptive batching window config for affected routes; enable guardrail cap on max_batch_wait_ms.

Hourglass timetable (72h watch + 7-day stabilization):
- Phase 0 — Preflight (T-48 to T-24)
  - Tasks: perf regression test run (nightly bench on dedicated pool), smoke PR merge, run eval harness (quality + perf).
  - Approvers: eng lead (Priya), SRE on-duty, product PM signoff.
  - Exit criteria: no perf regressions >3% P95; eval quality passes threshold; canary infra room reserved.

- Phase 1 — Micro-canary (T0 to T+3h) -> 0.5% global traffic (sparse geos)
  - Monitor: every 5m for first 30m, then 15m. Alert if P95 increase >10% or error rate > 3x baseline.
  - Rollback rule: auto-rollback if any single alert fires twice within 30m.

- Phase 2 — Soft ramp (T+3h to T+24h) -> 0.5% -> 3% -> 10% in steps
  - Each step: 3x stabilization window (30m), manual gate review at 3% and 10%.
  - Telemetry: evaluate model eval set hourly; run sampling of live responses for semantic drift (human-in-the-loop if flagged).

- Phase 3 — Broad observation (T+24h to T+72h) -> 10% -> 30% -> hold
  - 72h watch with 24/7 SRE coverage. Hold at 30% until no adverse trends for 48h.

- Phase 4 — Full rollout or staged rollback (T+72h onward)
  - If pass: ramp remaining traffic over 24h with rollback windows every +6h.
  - If fail: staged rollback starting with routes showing highest delta; fallback to last stable model variant and quant profile.

Staffing lattice (quick look):
- Preflight: 1 release lead (Priya), 1 runtime owner, 1 SRE, 1 QA engineer.
- Micro-canary: release lead + runtime owner on-call + SRE pager; 60m hot-seat.
- Soft ramp (first 24h): dedicated watch team (Priya, Ethan, Daria) in 8h staggered shifts; SRE pager rotation (primary/secondary).
- 72h watch: 24/7 SRE schedule; product/solutions on-call 09:00–21:00 UTC first 48h.

Observability checklist (pre-deploy):
- Dashboards: per-route P50/P95/P99, 5xx count, token-per-request distribution, runtime.queue_length_percentile_99, model fallback ratio.
- Alerts: set temporary sensitivity (x2 baseline) and a suppression policy for known noisy signals.
- Sampling: enable 1% live-response capture for affected routes and ship to review bucket.
- Logs: retain detailed runtime logs for 72h with rapid query templates (JQL snippets).
- Traces: ensure end-to-end traces include model-variant tag, quant_profile, kernel_path, and batch_size.

Release notes draft (for help center + customer comms):
- Title: Experimental q8-dyn quant profile + adaptive batching window (soft rollout)
- Short summary: We are gradually enabling a new quantization profile (q8-dyn) for model open-model-xyz and a minor adaptive batching window extension. Expected benefits: up to ~10% reduction in per-token GPU time in common cases and modest overall throughput improvement.
- Who it affects: Non-guaranteed hosted API users will see change first. Dedicated and Private customers may opt-in via config. There is no data retention change.
- Known limitations: In rare, prefix-heavy prompts, you may observe tail latency changes or small semantic differences; we are monitoring and will roll back if quality deviates.
- Rollback instructions (customer-facing): If you observe regressions, contact support@redwood.ai with subject line "q8-dyn regression" and include request-id and timing. Our incident team will evaluate and, if needed, pin your traffic to the last-stable variant.

Operational rollback decision tree (short form):
- Alert fired? Check impact scope (routes/customers).
  - Single route, single region: revert route config and monitor for 30m.
  - Multi-route or Dedicated customer affected: escalate to Release Lead + SRE lead; prepare immediate pin and customer communications.

Quick smoke-playbook (30m):
- 0–5m: detect alert and ack in pager duty. Capture sample request ids.
- 5–15m: check dashboards, confirm signal across telemetry. Decide one of: monitor, revert config, or rollback model variant.
- 15–30m: execute action (revert or pin) and update incident channel (#release-ops and #sre-watch).

Open questions / TODOs (owner: Priya):
- Decide sample size and threshold for semantic-diff auto-flagging (QA suggestion: 200 live samples with embedding distance > 0.22).
- Confirm Dedicated customer opt-in flow for q8-dyn (legal/contract implications).
- Add a runbook entry for kernel-path fallbacks (who pushes next-stable kernel).
- Schedule a short dry run with internal canary traffic (ticket: RELEASE-2123).

Links / references:
- Jira: RELEASE-2123 (rollout coordination), PERF-998 (bench results), QA-440 (eval harness).
- Confluence playbook (working): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/REL/Hourglass+Soft+Rollout+Playbook
- GitHub: platform PR #8742 (quant profile), infra PR #8791 (batching config).

Appendix — minimal telemetry thresholds (for automation rules):
- Global P95 increase trigger: >12% sustained for 15m.
- Route-level P95 trigger: >10% sustained for 10m.
- Error-rate trigger: 5xx rate > 4x baseline for 5m.
- Model-eval quality trigger: drop > 0.10 on curated prompt set or >2 prompts flagged by human reviewer.

Notes to self: keep this doc short and prescriptive. Will convert into a templated checklist for the release console once stabilized.
